name: Self-attention
summary: Every token attends to every other token, weighting them by learned query-key similarity.

name: Attention mechanism
summary: Let a decoder look back at the most relevant parts of the input instead of a single fixed vector.

name: Transformer
summary: A sequence model built entirely from attention and feed-forward layers, with no recurrence.

name: Residual connection
summary: Add a layer's input to its output so very deep networks stay trainable.

name: Batch normalization
summary: Normalise activations per mini-batch to stabilise and speed up training.

name: Deep ConvNet backbone
summary: Stacks of small convolutions as a general-purpose visual feature extractor.

name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
summary: Split an image into patches and feed them to a plain Transformer as a sequence of tokens.

name: Hierarchical / windowed ViT
summary: Attention inside local windows with multi-scale feature maps, so ViTs work for dense tasks.

name: Masked language modelling
summary: Hide some tokens and train the model to predict them from both sides of the context.

name: Autoregressive language modelling
summary: Train a model to predict the next token, so it can generate text left to right.

name: Contextual word embeddings
summary: Word vectors that depend on the surrounding sentence, from a pretrained language model.

name: Text-to-text framing
summary: Cast every task as text in, text out, so one model and one loss cover them all.

name: Unified LM via attention masks
summary: One shared Transformer does bidirectional, left-to-right and seq2seq modelling by switching attention masks.

name: In-context / few-shot learning
summary: A large model solves a new task from a few examples in its prompt, with no gradient updates.

name: Scaling laws
summary: Loss falls predictably with model size, data and compute, which tells you how to spend a budget.

name: Instruction tuning
summary: Fine-tune on many tasks phrased as natural-language instructions, so the model follows new instructions zero-shot.

name: RLHF
summary: Train a reward model on human preferences, then optimise the language model against it.

name: Open pretrained LLM
summary: Release large language model weights so the research community can build on them.

name: Contrastive image–text learning
summary: Pull matching image and caption embeddings together and push mismatched pairs apart.

name: Contrastive self-supervised vision
summary: Learn visual features without labels by matching augmented views of the same image.

name: Zero-shot transfer via text prompts
summary: Classify into unseen categories by comparing an image with text descriptions of the classes.

name: Web-scale image–text data
summary: Train on hundreds of millions of noisy image–caption pairs scraped from the web.

name: Weakly supervised pre-training
summary: Use huge amounts of cheap, noisy labels (hashtags, captions) instead of clean annotations.

name: Image–text matching (ITM)
summary: A binary classifier that decides whether an image and a caption actually match.

name: Cross-attention fusion
summary: Let text tokens attend to image features (and vice versa) to fuse the two modalities.

name: Single-stream VL Transformer
summary: Concatenate image regions and words and process them with one Transformer.

name: Object-detector region features
summary: Represent an image as features of detected object regions instead of a pixel grid.

name: Align before fuse
summary: Align unimodal image and text embeddings contrastively before fusing them with cross-attention.

name: Momentum distillation
summary: Learn from soft pseudo-targets produced by a moving-average copy of the model, to tolerate noisy web data.

name: Caption bootstrapping (CapFilt)
summary: Generate synthetic captions for web images and filter out noisy ones, then retrain on the cleaner data.

name: Multimodal mixture of encoder–decoder
aliases: unimodal encoder, image-grounded encoder and decoder
summary: One model that can act as a contrastive encoder, a matching encoder or a caption decoder.

name: Image-grounded text generation
summary: Train the model to generate the caption conditioned on the image.

name: Contrastive + captioning in one model
summary: Train one image–text model with both a contrastive loss and a captioning loss.

name: Frozen language model
summary: Keep a pretrained language model's weights fixed and teach only a small adapter to feed it visual information.

name: Frozen image encoder
summary: Keep a pretrained vision encoder fixed and train only the text or bridging side.

name: Visual prefix / soft prompt
summary: Turn an image into a few embedding vectors that a language model reads as if they were words.

name: Perceiver resampler
summary: A small set of learned queries cross-attends to many visual features and compresses them to a fixed number of tokens.

name: Gated cross-attention layers
summary: New cross-attention layers inserted into a frozen LLM, gated to start as an identity function.

name: Querying Transformer (Q-Former)
summary: A lightweight Transformer with learned queries that pulls the most text-relevant visual features out of a frozen image encoder.

name: Two-stage vision-to-language bootstrapping
summary: First teach the bridge to align vision and text, then teach it to talk to a frozen LLM.

name: Masked image modelling
summary: Hide image patches and train the model to predict them (or their visual tokens), the vision analogue of BERT.

name: Discrete visual tokens
summary: Compress images into a vocabulary of discrete codes so Transformers can model them like text.

name: Mixture of modality experts
summary: Shared attention with separate feed-forward experts per modality, so one Transformer handles image, text or both.

name: Decoupled weight decay (AdamW)
summary: Apply weight decay separately from the adaptive gradient step, which fixes how Adam regularises.

name: Large-batch training recipes
summary: Scale the learning rate with batch size and warm it up so huge batches train as well as small ones.

name: Model parallelism
summary: Split one giant model across many accelerators so it can be trained at all.

name: Visual question answering
summary: Answer free-form natural-language questions about an image.

name: Dense image–language annotation
summary: Human-written captions, regions and relationships that ground language in images.
